headline: Highest risk is broad data leakage and cascading errors from gpt-researcher’s browser/API/file access; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by godot_rl_agents’ no-network, non-runnable profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented I/O surfaces or network egress, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs by default. B can read files, browse, and use MCP, so if an operator manually bridges B’s reports into A’s workflow, injection becomes possible, but the pair lacks a default shared channel. This is lower severity because the pathway is unusual and A is non-runnable.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A’s control loop, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added between the agents, B content can reach A as untrusted input.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy B outputs into A prompts or configs.
Disable any shared MCP bridge between them.
Add a human review step before reusing B text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any bridged content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read local files and send content to external APIs, while A is documented with no network egress and no touched data classes. The pair does not show a shared workspace, but B’s default browser/API behavior creates a plausible leakage path for local documents or research artifacts if they are exposed to B. A is not the leak source here, but its outputs could still be copied into B manually.
conditions: IF local documents containing sensitive material are placed in B’s accessible workspace, B can transmit them to third-party APIs.
IF A’s outputs are manually imported into B’s research inputs, those contents may be uploaded by B.
mitigations: Restrict B to a sanitized folder.
Remove secrets from any files B can read.
Disable external API keys for nonessential runs.
Use a separate account or workspace for B.
requires-engineering: enforce file-level allowlists for B uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write, network, or filesystem surfaces, and is marked non-runnable, so it cannot materially contend with B over shared mutable resources by default. B can write via files, subprocesses, browsers, and package installs, but without a writable surface on A the overlap is mostly one-sided. Uncertainty is low because the missing A capabilities block the main conflict pathways.
conditions: IF A is later given filesystem or network write access to the same directory as B, write conflicts can occur.
IF both agents are run under a shared mutable workspace, B can overwrite artifacts A expects to remain stable.
mitigations: Keep A read-only or offline.
Run B in its own workspace.
Avoid shared git or package directories.
Serialize any writes through one agent at a time.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher stack and can treat upstream material as research input, while A is a game-playing agent with no documented verification or downstream action controls. If A’s outputs are fed into B, B may summarize or publish them without strong validation, creating a plausible cascade from A’s unverified content into B’s reports. The pathway exists in default B workflows, though not proven directly.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are used as source material for B’s research reports, B may propagate errors.
IF B is configured to publish without an explicit verification step, incorrect claims can cascade downstream.
mitigations: Require source verification before publication.
Mark A outputs as untrusted inputs.
Add a second-pass fact check in B.
Limit B to drafting only, not publishing.
requires-engineering: add citation provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, and B’s profile only shows general research tooling plus external APIs. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not directly evidenced and A has no touched data classes, the risk is limited to generic policy mismatch if sensitive data is introduced into B. I do not cite only B because the issue is pairwise exposure, but A contributes no specific compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed into B’s API-backed workflows, policy obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by B’s external services, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B.
Review API vendor terms before use.
Use redacted inputs for research runs.
Document retention settings for B.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for sensitive data.
